text: In thirteen twenty-four, a king walked into Cairo, and broke its economy.
sub: In 1324, a king walked into Cairo, and broke its economy.
asr: In 1324, a king walked into Cairo and broke its economy.

text: Not with an army. With gifts.
sub: Not with an army. With gifts.

text: His name was Mansa Musa, ruler of the Mali Empire, often called the richest man who ever lived.
sub: His name was Mansa Musa, ruler of the Mali Empire, often called the richest man who ever lived.

text: His kingdom was rich in gold, at a time when the whole world ran on it.
sub: His kingdom was rich in gold, at a time when the whole world ran on it.

text: That year, he set out for Mecca, across the Sahara.
sub: That year, he set out for Mecca, across the Sahara.

text: By some accounts, tens of thousands of people travelled with him, and camels loaded with gold.
sub: By some accounts, tens of thousands of people travelled with him, and camels loaded with gold.
asr: By some accounts, tens of thousands of people traveled with him and camels loaded with gold.

text: When he reached Cairo, he gave it away. To officials. To merchants. To the poor in the streets.
sub: When he reached Cairo, he gave it away. To officials. To merchants. To the poor in the streets.

text: There was so much gold in Cairo, that gold itself became cheap.
sub: There was so much gold in Cairo, that gold itself became cheap.

text: Its value fell. And according to one historian, twelve years later, it still hadn't recovered.
sub: Its value fell. And according to one historian, 12 years later, it still hadn't recovered.

text: One man's generosity shook one of the richest cities on Earth.
sub: One man's generosity shook one of the richest cities on Earth.

text: But it also put Mali on the map. Literally.
sub: But it also put Mali on the map. Literally.

text: Fifty years later, a famous map of the world showed him on a throne, holding a nugget of gold.
sub: 50 years later, a famous map of the world showed him on a throne, holding a nugget of gold.

text: Most people are remembered for what they kept. He was remembered for what he gave away.
sub: Most people are remembered for what they kept. He was remembered for what he gave away.
